title: Proof of trm hopf sigma1 sq closed form
html:
Proof. Proof of trm hopf sigma1 sq closed form

Proof

The Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_1^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_1 + 1 gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) = (q - q^{-1})\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) + \mathrm{tr}_M(1). The Markov axioms (rem:markov-axioms-primitive) fix \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z := q^3/(q^2+1) (convention D), so

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2)
  \;=\; (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \frac{q^3}{q^2 + 1} + 1.

Simplifying the first term: q - q^{-1} = (q^2-1)/q, so

  (q - q^{-1})\,z
  \;=\; \frac{q^2 - 1}{q} \cdot \frac{q^3}{q^2+1}
  \;=\; \frac{q^2(q^2-1)}{q^2+1}
  \;=\; \frac{q^2\,h}{[2]_q},

writing h = q - q^{-1} and [2]_q = q + q^{-1} = (q^2+1)/q. Adding 1 over the common denominator q^2+1 gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2)
  \;=\; \frac{q^2 + 1 + q^4 - q^2}{q^2+1}
  \;=\; \frac{q^4 + 1}{q^2 + 1}
  \;=\; \frac{q\,[2]_{q^2}}{[2]_q},

using q^4 + 1 = q^2 [2]_{q^2} and q^2 + 1 = q\,[2]_q. No half-integral power of q appears; the result is rational in q.

Corrected 2026-08-09. This derivation previously ran on the excised convention C, z = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}), where (q-q^{-1})z collapses to q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2} and the answer is 1 + (q-1)/q^{1/2}. That collapse — and with it every half-power in the old statement — is a property of C alone: it works because q - q^{-1} factors as (q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2})(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) and C is the reciprocal of the second factor. Under D no such cancellation occurs and none is needed.

Stabilisation (rem:markov-axioms-primitive axiom 3 and its \sigma_n^{-1} consequence) scales the trace by z for an adjoined positive crossing and by z_{-} = z - (q - q^{-1}) for a negative one. Neither case arises here: \sigma_1^2 involves only the first generator, and the Markov trace is compatible with the tower inclusions H_2(q) \subset H_n(q), so its trace in H_n for any n \geq 2 coincides with the trace in H_2 — no stabilisation factor enters because no new crossing is adjoined. ∎

Taylor expansion at q = 1 + \varepsilon

Split off the polynomial part by division:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) - 1
  \;=\; \frac{q^4 - q^2}{q^2+1}
  \;=\; q^2 - 2 + \frac{2}{q^2+1}.

Substituting q = 1 + \varepsilon, the polynomial part contributes \varepsilon^2 + 2\varepsilon - 1 and the rational part expands about a pair of conjugate poles at q = \pm i, i.e. \varepsilon = -1 \pm i:

  \bigl[\varepsilon^k\bigr]\,\frac{2}{q^2+1}
  \;=\; (-1)^k\,2^{(1-k)/2}\,
        \sin\!\Bigl(\tfrac{(k+1)\pi}{4}\Bigr),
        \qquad k \geq 0 .

So the series is a damped oscillation of period 8 in k, with radius of convergence \sqrt 2, rather than a binomial series. Its coefficients:

See Table 1.

Withdrawn 2026-08-09. Under the excised convention C this expansion was the closed binomial series \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^2) - 1 = \varepsilon\,(1+\varepsilon)^{-1/2} = \sum_{k \geq 0} \binom{-1/2}{k}\varepsilon^{k+1}, with coefficients 1, -\tfrac12, \tfrac38, -\tfrac5{16}, \tfrac{35}{128}, -\tfrac{63}{256}, \tfrac{231}{1024}, \ldots and radius of convergence 1 (branch point at q = 0). Both the binomial form and those coefficients are convention-C artefacts and are withdrawn; the D coefficients above are exact rationals derived symbolically from the corrected closed form. The numerical check that used to sit here — probe_F_n_categorical_derivation.py (witness, 2/2 assertions pass) — validated the C coefficients and has not been re-run under D; regenerating it is a producer change, not an edit.
